newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to invest HUF 1.1 bln in new mortgage bank.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to invest HUF 1.1 bln in new mortgage bank.

text.p: The government will contribute 1.1 billion forints in the third quarter of 1997 to the foundation of the first mortgage bank in Hungary since World War Two, a government spokesman said on Thursday.

"We do not know when exactly the bank will be set up, but the government will urge that as this will be a very important new institution," Elemer Kiss told a news conference following the cabinet meeting.

Kiss said the Land Credit and Mortgage Bank's registered capital would be three billion forints and the part above the state contribution would be put together by commercial banks, including Postabank, K&H Bank and Magyar Fejlesztesi Bank.

The new bank, which will revive a pre-war tradition, should strengthen economic growth by providing long-term loans now lacked on the Hungarian market and will be the first issuer of mortgage bonds, the government said.
"Besides satisfying the agricultural sector's demands, the bank will focus on mortgage loans covered by flats and commercial estates," it said.
